title: IP addressing & network data
outcome: Use standard address models and retain routing context.

steps.title: 1. Address, network or interface?
steps.text: ip_address models a host address. ip_network models a prefix. ip_interface represents an address together with its connected prefix. Choose the object that matches your question.

steps.title: 2. Normalize explicitly
steps.text: strict=False allows ip_network to clear supplied host bits. strict=True rejects them. State which behavior is intended rather than silently changing input.

steps.title: 3. Use scope and context
steps.text: Identical private addresses can exist in different routing contexts. Compare canonical addresses AND the explicit context. These drills never query real equipment.

steps.title: 4. Avoid IPv4 assumptions
steps.text: IPv6 has no broadcast address in the IPv4 sense. hosts() handles special prefix cases such as IPv4 /31 according to the library contract. Read the documentation rather than subtracting two unconditionally.

steps.title: 5. Treat results as defined checks
steps.text: An overlap check is a mathematical observation. Whether overlap is acceptable depends on the design. Exercises specify scope, permitted inputs and expected output.

Compare the implementation with case 04-prefix not address. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.
